blocks.text: UX Researcher — Psychology & Neuroscience

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Psychology, Humanities & Social Sciences
QUALIFICATION
Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies
Psychology & Neuroscience
CAREER LEVEL
Entry-level
UX Research Intern / Junior UX Researcher, subject to employer requirements

A User Experience (UX) Researcher studies how people interact with websites, mobile applications, digital products, and services. The goal is to understand users' needs, motivations, behaviours, frustrations, and expectations so product teams can make better design and business decisions.
A Psychology & Neuroscience background is relevant because it develops an understanding of human behaviour, cognition, attention, memory, perception, decision-making, and research methods.

UX research is different from UX design: researchers primarily investigate user problems and test experiences, while designers focus on creating and refining solutions. In some organisations, the responsibilities overlap.

Career progression
Year 1
Foundation
Understand human behaviour

items.text: Study introductory psychology, cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and social psychology.
Learn research ethics, observation, and scientific reasoning.
Understand perception, attention, memory, motivation, and decision-making.
Practise academic writing, note-taking, and evidence evaluation.
Observe usability problems in everyday apps and websites.

blocks.text: Year 2
Methods
Learn UX research techniques

items.text: Practise user interviews, contextual inquiry, surveys, and observation.
Learn qualitative coding, thematic analysis, and research synthesis.
Study experimental design, sampling, bias, reliability, and validity.
Learn descriptive statistics and introductory inferential statistics.
Understand usability testing, accessibility, and human-computer interaction (HCI).
Conduct a small study on a website or mobile application.

blocks.text: Year 3
Application
Build a UX research portfolio

items.text: Conduct moderated usability tests and analyse the findings.
Learn survey design, participant recruitment, and research planning.
Practise presenting insights to designers, developers, and product managers.
Create two or three detailed case studies.
Seek UX research internships, research assistant positions, or product research projects.
Explore specialised areas such as accessibility, healthcare UX, or consumer behaviour.

blocks.text: Year 4
If applicable
Prepare for employment or postgraduate study

items.text: Complete a thesis, capstone project, or applied UX research study.
Develop an end-to-end case study from research question to recommendations.
Practise research presentations and explaining methodological limitations.
Apply for graduate and junior research roles.
Consider a master's in HCI, UX research, cognitive science, or a related field if needed for the intended roles.

blocks.text: Adapt the plan to the duration and curriculum of the chosen programme. A three-year degree can cover the same foundations and projects in a compressed schedule.

rows.text: Makes insights useful to product teams
Working with designers, engineers, and product managers

blocks.text: Interface and prototype review
Figma — inspect interfaces, review prototypes, and collaborate with product designers.
Research planning and documentation
Notion or spreadsheets — organise research plans, interview notes, participant information, and findings.
Survey and quantitative analysis
Google Forms or Qualtrics for surveys; Excel, Google Sheets, or SPSS for data analysis, depending on access and project requirements.
Usability testing
Explore platforms such as Maze and Useberry to understand prototype testing and task-based research workflows. Free access and feature limits vary.
Behavioural data
Learn introductory SQL and a product analytics tool such as Google Analytics for roles that combine qualitative research with product usage data.

You do not need to master every tool before applying. Strong research methodology, ethical practice, analytical reasoning, and a clear portfolio are more important than collecting tool certifications.
Aim to complete at least three projects that demonstrate different research methods.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Mobile app usability study

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Usability testing
Select a familiar app, such as a food delivery, travel, or education app. Ask a small group of consenting participants to complete clearly defined tasks.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Research plan, task script, observed usability issues, prioritised findings, and improvement recommendations.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: User interviews and thematic analysis

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Qualitative research
Investigate a question such as why students abandon online courses or find job-search platforms difficult to use.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Interview guide, anonymised notes, coding framework, recurring themes, and evidence-backed insights.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Survey-based user research

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Quantitative research
Design a survey to understand user preferences or barriers in a digital service. Define the target population and acknowledge sampling limitations.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Survey instrument, data-cleaning notes, charts, findings, and recommendations supported by the collected data.

For every case study, include the research question, your role, methodology, participant selection, findings, limitations, and how the findings could influence product decisions. Never invent participant quotes or claim that proposed improvements produced measured results when they have not been tested.

blocks.text: These are potential places to explore, not confirmations of current vacancies. Research roles can be competitive, and some employers prefer candidates with a master's degree or prior applied research experience.
How to improve your chances:

items.text: Build a concise portfolio with two or three well-explained case studies.
Demonstrate both qualitative and quantitative research skills.
Learn to present findings as product decisions, not just lists of observations.
Network with UX researchers and seek feedback on your work.
Apply to adjacent research, consumer-insights, and product-analyst roles as well.

rows.text: Interaction design, human factors, usability principles
Cognitive psychology, social psychology, behavioural science
Sampling, ethics, validity, qualitative and quantitative methods
Statistics, Excel, introductory R or Python where relevant
Research storytelling, report writing, stakeholder presentations

blocks.text: Look for reputable university courses and established professional training. Treat certificates as supporting evidence of learning, not substitutes for demonstrated research ability.
A postgraduate qualification may expand opportunities for specialist or research-intensive positions.
Master's in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)
Closely aligned with usability, interaction, user research, and the design of digital systems.
Master's in Cognitive Science or Cognitive Psychology
Useful for deeper study of attention, memory, decision-making, perception, and human behaviour.
Master's in Psychology or Research Methods
Can strengthen behavioural research, experimental design, and statistical analysis. Check programme eligibility and any professional-practice requirements.
Human Factors, Ergonomics, or Interaction Design
Appropriate for research on usability, safety, accessibility, and the interaction between people and technology.

rows.text: Assist with interviews, testing, documentation, and analysis
Plan and conduct studies; synthesise findings; communicate insights
Lead complex studies and influence product strategy
Set research priorities, mentor researchers, coordinate teams
Director of UX Research / Research specialist
Shape research strategy, organisational practice, and high-impact decisions

blocks.text: Some professionals also specialise in behavioural science, consumer insights, accessibility research, human factors, or product analytics.
UX researchers may increasingly work on:

blocks.label: AI product research
blocks.text: Understanding trust, usability, transparency, and user expectations around AI-powered systems.

blocks.label: Healthcare UX
blocks.text: Studying patient portals, telehealth, and digital health workflows.

blocks.label: Accessibility research
blocks.text: Investigating how people with different abilities use digital products.

blocks.label: Conversational interfaces
blocks.text: Testing chatbots, voice assistants, and AI agents.

blocks.label: Behavioural insights
blocks.text: Applying psychology to understand decision-making and product usage.

blocks.label: Responsible technology
blocks.text: Researching privacy expectations, consent, and unintended user harms.
These are areas to explore, not guarantees of employment growth.
Use this self-assessment to track readiness for entry-level UX research opportunities.
UX research readiness tracker
I understand basic cognitive and social psychology.
I can plan and conduct a user interview without leading the participant.
I can run a basic usability test and document observed issues.
I can organise qualitative notes and identify recurring themes.
I can analyse survey results using spreadsheets and basic statistics.
I understand research ethics, informed consent, and participant privacy.
I have at least two documented UX research case studies.
I can present findings and prioritised recommendations to a product team.
I have tailored my CV and portfolio for relevant internships or junior roles.
Check off each item as you develop the skill. This is a preparation guide, not a hiring guarantee.
By graduation, a competitive candidate should be able to:

items.text: Explain how psychology and neuroscience inform user behaviour.
Select appropriate qualitative and quantitative research methods.
Conduct ethical user interviews, surveys, and usability tests.
Analyse findings and distinguish evidence from assumptions.
Translate research into clear, prioritised product recommendations.
Present a portfolio demonstrating the complete research process.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Begin with user interviews and usability testing, then learn qualitative analysis and basic statistics. Complete two or three credible case studies before applying for UX Research Intern, Research Assistant, or Junior UX Researcher positions.
